messages:
maria_cs: Heads-up: HelioWorks dedicated pool bring-up tomorrow 09:00 PT. Need final quota confirmation + autoscale knobs before warmup. Renewal health depends on smooth first 48h.
kenny_infra: @maria_cs I have the reservation ID and GPU pool ready. Quota currently set to 250k tokens/minute aggregated. Can bump to 350k for the first 24h if we expect higher burst.
sophia_pm: Renewal note: customer flagged strict p95 latency target of 180ms. They're doing a gating demo Tuesday. 
alex_runtime: p95 180ms is tight with current model (gpt-large-8k). Suggest enabling KV prefix caching + continuous batching. Also have a quantized variant (q4f32) we can flip to for fallback.
maria_cs: Can we write a short plan for the ramp and a rollback checklist? I want to share with CS and the customer's SREs.
kenny_infra: Plan sketch:
- 09:00 PT: Enable reserved pool + route 10% traffic (canary)
- 09:30 PT: Increase to 40% if p95 < 220ms and error < 0.5%
- 10:30 PT: Full switch if metrics look good
- Autoscale policy: target util 65%, max burst 2x reserved
- Fallback sequence: q4 -> smaller context -> lower batch size

alex_runtime: Loadtest snippet for their traffic profile (k6):
```bash
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 15m --rps 800 --out json=helio-k6.json loadtest_script.js
```
Use header X-Helio-Test: smoke to ensure we hit priming cache.

sophia_pm: Adding renewal risk notes: If we can't hit p95 180ms for demo, escalate to AE for SLA concession. But let's avoid that.
maria_cs: Who will run the loadtest and monitor? I'll coordinate with customer SREs.
kenny_infra: I'll kick the loadtest at 08:00 PT for a dry run. Alex, please monitor runtime metrics and trace IDs. deploy-bot: deploy scheduled for 2024-04-07T09:00:00-07:00.
alex_runtime: Monitoring checklist: p95 latency, error rate, token throughput, GPU mem pressure, KV hit ratio. Alerts: p95 > 250ms for 3m -> rollback.
maria_cs: Good. Also capturing enablement feedback: need a 1 pager for the customer's infra team explaining how autoscale works and how to interpret the cache hit metric. I'll draft.
kenny_infra: One more: quota enforcement config is soft for first 3 hours (throttling with 429 backoff window 30s) so customer load won't be dropped hard during warmup.
sophia_pm: Please note any regressions vs baseline eval set. If quality drops when switching to q4, we need approval before full flip.
alex_runtime: I'll prepare an eval run: run 1k prompts from their eval set under q4 and baseline and post diffs. Expected latency improvement ~18% at cost of minor n-gram shifts.
maria_cs: Thanks. After dry run I'll share a single doc with timeline + who owns each step. If anything deviates, ping here and @sophia_pm.
kenny_infra: Dry run logs (snippet):
```
[08:05:12] loadgen: rps=780, errored=2 (0.26%), p95=198ms
[08:10:12] runtime: kv_hit=0.42, gpu_util=58%, mem_free=14GB
```
Looks okay.
maria_cs: Awesome. Tagging next steps: alex prepares eval diffs by 06:00 PT, kenny does dry run 08:00 PT, I'll send customer timeline by 12:00 PT.
deploy-bot: NOTE: incident playbook quicklink -> https://redwood.internal/playbooks/dedicated-warmup
alex_runtime: If anyone wants to sanity-check the autoscale JSON, here's the policy to apply: `{"target_util":65,"max_multiplier":2,"scale_window_s":120}`
kenny_infra: I'll apply that at 08:50 PT for the canary window.
maria_cs: Thanks team. I'll close the loop after the dry run and post the final timeline here. :thumbsup:
